# What an MCP server's tool list costs: we counted the tokens of 34,374 of them

#opensource #ai #llm #mcp

Under our survey of 12,915 MCP servers, a reader did the arithmetic we had not: 182,157 tool definitions over 7,656 servers is about 24 tools each, and a client resends every one of them with each model request. Count the tokens of a typical list, the comment said, and that becomes a cost.

HISTOR, our public log of MCP servers, keeps the current tool list of every server it observes. So instead of one typical list we counted all of them: 18,204 npm and PyPI packages and 16,170 remote servers, as of 19 October 2026.

## How we counted

A list is counted the way a client puts it into a model request: for each tool its `name`, `description` and `input_schema`, as compact JSON. The tokenizer is `o200k_base` (tiktoken 0.12). Every server with at least one tool counts once, with the list HISTOR last observed.

## The numbers

 | Packages  | Remote servers
--- | --- | ---
Servers  | 18,204  | 16,170
Tool definitions  | 337,449  | 232,427
Tools per server: median / mean  | 8 / 18.5  | 7 / 14.4
Tokens per server: median  | 1,272  | 1,328
mean  | 3,812  | 3,412
90th percentile  | 8,361  | 7,425
99th percentile  | 39,612  | 22,294
largest  | 304,780  | 547,935
Tokens per tool: median  | 129  | 231
Servers over 10,000 tokens  | 1,447  | 618
Servers over 100,000 tokens  | 31  | 9

Three things stand out.

The mean is three times the median. A typical server is cheap. A few hundred servers with hundreds or thousands of tools carry most of the tokens. The "about 24 tools" from the survey was the mean over the packages that answered on 13 October; over today's larger set the mean is 18.5 and the median 8.

The heaviest lists are not the ones with the most tools. The largest remote list is 547,935 tokens for 71 tools, about 7,700 tokens per tool. Another remote server lists 15 tools in 175,588 tokens. What makes a list heavy is the size of each definition more than the number of tools: at thousands of tokens per tool, a description or an input schema is a document of its own.

Some do not fit at all. 304,780 tokens is more than a 200,000-token context window. A client that connects that package has no room left for the question.

## In money

The list rides along with every request, so its cost is tokens × price × requests. Per 1,000 requests at list prices on 19 October 2026:

One server's list  | Tokens  | $0.10 per million (a small model)  | $2 per million (a mid-size model)  | The mid-size model reading it from a prompt cache
--- | --- | --- | --- | ---
median package  | 1,272  | $0.13  | $2.54  | $0.13
mean package  | 3,812  | $0.38  | $7.62  | $0.38
90th percentile  | 8,361  | $0.84  | $16.72  | $0.84
99th percentile  | 39,612  | $3.96  | $79.22  | $3.96

A client with five median servers sends about 6,400 tokens of tool definitions before the user types a word.

## What cuts the bill

  * Prompt caching. If the client keeps the tool list identical and early in the prompt, a cached read costs about a twentieth of the input price. A client that reorders tools, or rebuilds the list per request, gives that up.
  * Loading definitions on demand. The model sees tool names first and gets a schema only when it is about to call that tool.
  * For publishers: smaller definitions. A description that says what the tool does and when to use it, and nothing more. Schemas without repeated prose. Fewer tools, or related operations behind one tool with an `action` argument. The median tool is 129 tokens in a package and 231 on a remote server; at 7,700 tokens per tool, something else is going on.

## Count yours

We put the counter on a free page: modelmarket.dev/tools/tool-list-cost. Paste a `tools/list`, or name a server HISTOR observes (an https endpoint, `npm:<package>`, `pypi:<package>` or a registry name). You get its tokens, where it sits among the 34,374, the money per 1,000 requests, the heaviest tools, and a line for your README:
    
    `![tool list](https://img.shields.io/endpoint?url=https%3A%2F%2Fmodelmarket.dev%2Ftools%2Fbadge%2Ftool-list-cost%3Fserver%3Dnpm%253Ayour-package)
    `

The page counts with the same tokenizer as the numbers above. We checked it against tiktoken on 120 of HISTOR's tool lists, 2.6 million tokens, with no difference. A pasted list is counted in memory and not kept; a lookup asks HISTOR and never contacts the server.

## What this does not measure

  * One tokenizer. Other models count differently, typically by tens of percent. The shape carries over: a median near 1,300 tokens and a long tail.
  * The provider's own text. A model API wraps tool definitions in its own instructions; those are not counted.
  * What clients really send. Some drop fields or shorten long descriptions; some also send the output schema. Counted as listed in full, a package's list has a median of 1,390 tokens and a 90th percentile of 9,960.
  * Which servers people use. Every listed server counts once. A popular server and an abandoned one weigh the same.

## Reproduce

The method, in five languages, is docs/tool-list-cost.md in alexar76/histor, with the script that counted (`scripts/tool_list_tokens.py`, export query in its docstring) and the summary without server names (`docs/tool-list-tokens-2026-10-19.json`).

We build HISTOR and WARDEN. The numbers are a snapshot of 19 October 2026; the log keeps moving. No server is named here. Thanks to Paul Irolla for the question.--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
